data.narrative:
Destinus is a late-stage defense and security company that has raised over $400M to date. The valuation universe comprises 26 same-sector peers, including 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms at adjacent stages; notable private comparables include Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and Saronic.

The peer-median method was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or similar-tier datapoints within the narrow defense cohort—only 0 same-stage and 2 adjacent-stage peers met filter criteria, falling short of the 3-company minimum for reliable triangulation. Consequently, analysis relies on the stage-progression method, which applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage advancement to the $400M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $480M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $408M to $552M, centered on $480M, derived from a single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 1.2x late-stage multiplier for defense-tech specifically and the absence of direct peer benchmarking due to limited comparables at Destinus's valuation tier. Broader application of the 26-company defense sector median or use of public comps would introduce additional noise. A multi-method triangulation would require access to a denser network of same-stage private defense companies or normalizing against the wider sector peer set.
